units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
Lord Goring merely rang that you should show me out. Good-night, Lord Goring!
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Goes out followed by PHIPPS.
Her face is illumined with evil triumph .
There is joy in her eyes .
Youth seems to have come back to her .
Her last glance is like a swift arrow .
LORD GORING bites his lip , and lights a cigarette .
FOURTH ACT
Same as Act II .
LORD GORING is standing by the fireplace with his hands in his pockets .
He is looking rather bored .
Pulls out his watch , inspects it , and rings the bell .
It is a great nuisance. I can’t find any one in this house to talk to. And I am full of interesting information. I feel like the latest edition of something or other.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Enter servant .
Sir Robert is still at the Foreign Office, my lord.
units.name: JAMES

units.text: Lady Chiltern not down yet?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Her ladyship has not yet left her room. Miss Chiltern has just come in from riding.
units.name: JAMES

units.text: To himself .
Ah! that is something.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Lord Caversham has been waiting some time in the library for Sir Robert. I told him your lordship was here.
units.name: JAMES

units.text: Thank you! Would you kindly tell him I’ve gone?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Bowing .
I shall do so, my lord.
units.name: JAMES

units.text: Exit servant .

Really, I don’t want to meet my father three days running. It is a great deal too much excitement for any son. I hope to goodness he won’t come up. Fathers should be neither seen nor heard. That is the only proper basis for family life. Mothers are different. Mothers are darlings.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Throws himself down into a chair , picks up a paper and begins to read it .
Enter LORD CAVERSHAM.
Well, sir, what are you doing here? Wasting your time as usual, I suppose?
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Throws down paper and rises .
My dear father, when one pays a visit it is for the purpose of wasting other people’s time, not one’s own.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Have you been thinking over what I spoke to you about last night?
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: I have been thinking about nothing else.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Engaged to be married yet?
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Genially .
Not yet: but I hope to be before lunch-time.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Caustically .
You can have till dinner-time if it would be of any convenience to you.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Thanks awfully, but I think I’d sooner be engaged before lunch.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Humph! Never know when you are serious or not.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Neither do I, father.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: A pause .
I suppose you have read The Times this morning?
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Airily .
The Times? Certainly not. I only read The Morning Post . All that one should know about modern life is where the Duchesses are; anything else is quite demoralising.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Do you mean to say you have not read The Times leading article on Robert Chiltern’s career?
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Good heavens! No. What does it say?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: What should it say, sir? Everything complimentary, of course. Chiltern’s speech last night on this Argentine Canal scheme was one of the finest pieces of oratory ever delivered in the House since Canning.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Ah! Never heard of Canning. Never wanted to. And did . . . did Chiltern uphold the scheme?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Uphold it, sir? How little you know him! Why, he denounced it roundly, and the whole system of modern political finance. This speech is the turning-point in his career, as The Times points out. You should read this article, sir.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Opens The Times.

‘Sir Robert Chiltern . . . most rising of our young statesmen . . . Brilliant Orator . . . Unblemished career . . . Well-known integrity of character . . . Represents what is best in English public life . . . Noble contrast to the lax morality so common among foreign politicians.’ They will never say that of you, sir.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM
